title: Warm thyme grapes and goat's cheese on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Goat's cheese, walnuts, honey, butter, bread and grapes are all plain whole foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Soft goat's cheese, walnuts and red grapes are everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan and a toaster or grill, with simple toasting and pan-frying.

works.reason: 300g grapes, 150g goat's cheese and four thick slices make a sensible breakfast for four, and 4 to 5 minutes in butter is enough to burst the grapes.

honest_times.reason: Picking grapes and thyme, chopping walnuts and spreading toast fits 12 minutes, and 3 plus 5 minutes in the pan matches the 8 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the thyme and black pepper, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm, jammy grapes are the centre of a cosy late-November breakfast.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and written in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Toast with cheese, walnuts and fruit gives protein, fat and fruit, a proper breakfast a family would happily eat again.
